quickAnswer.title: Quick answer
quickAnswer.body: Need a gardener in Newquay? Start with the type of job, then compare public service details, prices, proof, insurance and waste information. Quilliams appears first because this is my own website, not because an independent panel ranked it first. For domestic lawn mowing, hedge trimming, recurring garden maintenance, one-off tidy-ups and practical landscaping, I recommend asking Quilliams for a quote alongside any provider whose public focus fits the work. I am based near Newquay, show local project proof, carry public liability insurance, and Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202. The comparison below was checked against direct provider websites or the linked public listing on 27 July 2026. Where a provider did not publish a price, insurance detail or waste status on the page checked, the table says “Not publicly stated” rather than guessing.

sections.title: Why I put Quilliams first
sections.body:
Quilliams Gardening & Landscaping is best suited to homeowners in Newquay who want reliable lawn mowing, hedge trimming, garden maintenance, seasonal clearances, waste removal and practical landscaping from an owner-operated local gardener. I am based in Trevarrian, a few minutes from Newquay, so this is my home patch rather than a distant service area I mention for search traffic.

The jobs I am strongest on are the domestic ones that make a garden feel usable again: overgrown lawns, hedges that have got too wide, rental or holiday-let tidy-ups, low-maintenance gravel areas, and regular maintenance for people who do not want to chase a gardener every fortnight. I am not the right fit for agricultural field mowing, baling, large tree surgery, or heavy construction landscaping.

sections.title: How this Newquay gardener comparison was built
sections.body:
I included providers that had a live direct website or a specific public business listing, described work relevant to Newquay or the surrounding area, and gave enough public information to compare at least their service focus. This is a practical shortlist, not an exhaustive directory. It was checked on 27 July 2026 and should be rechecked quarterly because services, prices and availability change.

I did not mystery-shop the businesses, verify every review, inspect insurance certificates, or test the quality of their work. The matrix reports what each linked source publicly stated on the check date. It does not turn missing website detail into a negative claim, and it uses “Not publicly stated” whenever the source did not answer a field. Quilliams is listed first because this article is published by Quilliams and the commercial relationship must be obvious; readers should still compare current quotes and ask each provider for evidence relevant to their job.
bullets: Inclusion: a live provider source plus a publicly stated Newquay or relevant Cornwall service.
Evidence: direct provider websites where available; a named directory listing only where no direct site was identified.
No hidden score: providers are not ranked by unverified reviews, popularity or claimed quality.
Freshness: checked 27 July 2026; review the linked source again before booking.

sections.title: How to compare gardeners in Newquay
sections.body:
The best gardener is the one that fits your garden, budget and expectations. Start by looking for proof that the business actually works in Newquay. Project photos, named neighbourhoods, recent reviews, and clear service-area wording all help. A provider does not need to publish every business document on its website, but it should answer reasonable questions before work starts.

Ask about insurance and waste handling before you book. Garden waste should not be left unclear in the quote, and householders should check that anyone taking waste is appropriately authorised for the arrangement. A good quote should say what is included, what happens with clippings, whether access is a problem, whether repeat visits are available, and what would change the price. That protects both sides and avoids awkward conversations after the job starts.
bullets: Choose a maintenance gardener for mowing, weeding, pruning, tidy-ups and hedge maintenance.
Choose a landscaper for layout changes, planting schemes, turfing, gravel gardens and larger improvements.
Choose a qualified tree surgeon for large tree work, climbing work or anything involving serious height and risk.

sections.title: Best fit by job type
sections.body:
For regular lawn mowing, Quilliams or another local maintenance gardener is usually the right fit. Check frequency, edging, clippings, minimum visit charge and whether winter visits are available. Cornwall lawns often grow longer into autumn than people expect, so a flexible schedule is useful.

For hedge trimming, check height, access, nesting season, waste removal and price per metre. Normal domestic hedges are well within my work, but very tall hedges, tree-like conifers, and anything requiring climbing equipment may need a specialist. For one-off garden cleanups, send photos from a few angles. Waste volume and access make the biggest difference to cost. For field mowing, baling or agricultural hedges, speak to an agricultural contractor rather than a domestic gardener.
bullets: Regular lawn mowing: check edging, clippings, schedule and minimum visit charge.
Hedge trimming: check height, access, nesting season and green waste.
One-off tidy-up: check waste volume, bramble, access and what is left at the end.
Large tree work: check qualifications, climbing cover and insurance.

sections.title: A closer look at Green Guys, GreenFern and Quilliams
sections.body:
If you are specifically comparing Green Guys, GreenFern Garden Services and Quilliams Gardening & Landscaping, start with the job type. Checked on 27 July 2026, Green Guys publicly presented itself as a Newquay home and garden service covering general gardening, grass cutting, hedge trimming, weed control, pressure washing, property management, painting and car washing, with hourly gardener pricing shown on its website. That may suit someone who wants broader home-care help as well as garden tasks.

GreenFern publicly listed Newquay services including lawn mowing, lawn care, garden clearance, pressure washing, weed control, turfing, fencing and garden maintenance. Its website advertised instant quotes and booking, professional invoicing and a 10-mile Newquay service radius. That may appeal to landlords, holiday-let hosts and homeowners who want a digital booking route. Insurance and waste details were not publicly stated on the pages checked, so ask GreenFern directly rather than assuming either way.

Quilliams is positioned slightly differently. I am not trying to cover every home-care job. The strongest fit is domestic garden maintenance, lawn mowing, hedge trimming, one-off tidy-ups and practical low-maintenance landscaping around Newquay and north Cornwall. If you want owner-operated communication, visible local project proof, public liability insurance, Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202, and a quote based on photos or a short site visit, Quilliams is the option I would put forward first.

sections.title: Questions to ask before booking
sections.body:
Before booking a gardener in Newquay, ask five simple questions. Are you insured? Do you remove green waste, and how is it disposed of? What exactly is included in the quote? How soon can you do the work? Do you offer regular visits if I want to keep the garden under control afterwards?

The answers tell you a lot. Clear, practical answers usually mean the person has done the work often enough to know what can go wrong. Vague answers are a warning sign, especially around access, waste and scope. I would rather tell someone upfront that a job is bigger than it looks than promise a low price and have it become uncomfortable later. Good gardening is partly about the finish, but it is also about communication.
